root_causes.description: product-catalog is consuming ~2.0 CPU cores while every peer service sits at <=0.02 cores, saturating its CPU and inflating response times toward the 10s timeout ceiling. Because frontend, checkout, and recommendation all depend on product-catalog (checkout -> product-catalog, frontend -> product-catalog, recommendation -> product-catalog), their p99 latency is driven to 10000ms, producing the high-latency alert.

evidence.expected_baseline: peer services same window: frontend=0.014, recommendation=0.012, checkout=0.002 cores
no memory growth; rules out memory_stress

root_causes.description: frontend p99 is pinned at the 10s ceiling across user-facing operations; this is a propagated symptom of the product-catalog CPU saturation rather than a frontend-internal fault, since frontend CPU and memory are normal and it has no errors.

checkout p99 is at 10000ms with slow spans, but its own CPU/memory are normal and all other downstream dependencies (payment, shipping, cart, currency, email) are healthy, so the latency is inherited from the slow product-catalog dependency.

evidence.observed_value: user_checkout_single span duration=28135ms, status ok, 0 errors

remediation_steps: Inspect per-pod CPU throttling (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total) and node pressure for product-catalog pod (product-catalog-5bb7676754-hcfpv) to confirm CPU saturation.
Scale product-catalog horizontally and/or raise its CPU limit to relieve the ~2-core saturation so p99 returns below 100ms.
If externally induced, disable the CPU-stress fault injection on product-catalog (chaos/flagd target) and confirm CPU returns to <0.05 cores.
Verify frontend, checkout, and recommendation p99 recover once product-catalog is healthy.
